questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Triple Integral Using the Product Rule
questions.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{z{sec}^{2}⁡x}{y}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-\frac{\pi }{4}\le x\le \frac{\pi }{3},\,{e}^{2}\le y\le {e}^{5},\,0\le z\le 4}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{z{sec}^{2}⁡x}{y}\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{5}}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}\frac{z{sec}^{2}⁡x}{y}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[-\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{\pi }{3}]\times [{e}^{2},{e}^{5}]\times [0,4]$ is a rectangular box, and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{5}}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}\frac{z{sec}^{2}⁡x}{y}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{5}}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}{sec}^{2}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{y}\cdot z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}{sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{5}}\frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{0}^{4}z\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}{sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{5}}\frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{0}^{4}z\,\text{d}z & =[\operatorname{tan}⁡x]_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}\cdot [\operatorname{ln}⁡y]_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{5}}\cdot {[\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{4} \\  & =(\sqrt{3}+1)\cdot (5-2)\cdot (8-0) \\  & =(\sqrt{3}+1)\cdot 3\cdot 8 \\  & =24(\sqrt{3}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{{3}^{y-1}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{z-4}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,\frac{\pi }{3}\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le 1,\,5\le z\le 7}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{{3}^{y-1}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{z-4}\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{5}^{7}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\frac{{3}^{y-1}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{z-4}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{2}]\times [0,1]\times [5,7]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{5}^{7}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\frac{{3}^{y-1}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{z-4}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{5}^{7}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\frac{{3}^{y-1}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x}{z-4}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{1}{3}^{y-1}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{5}^{7}\frac{1}{z-4}\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{1}{3}^{y-1}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{5}^{7}\frac{1}{z-4}\,\text{d}z & =[-\operatorname{cos}⁡x]_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\cdot {[\frac{{3}^{y-1}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}]}_{0}^{1}\cdot [\operatorname{ln}⁡(z-4)]_{5}^{7} \\  & =(-0+\frac{1}{2})\cdot (\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡3-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By integrating first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ and then $z,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}z+\frac{1}{y}\,dV
$$

over the rectangular box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,1\le y\le 3,\,-1\le z\le 1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}z+\frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}z+\frac{1}{y}\,dy\,dx\,dz
$$

Since we're integrating first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ and then $z,$ we write $\text{d}V=\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}z+\frac{1}{y}\,dy\,dx\,dz & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}z+\frac{1}{y}\,dy]dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{x}^{2}zy+\operatorname{ln}⁡|y|]_{y=1}^{y=3}\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}z(3-1)+(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-0)\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}2{x}^{2}z+\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,dx\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $z$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}2{x}^{2}z+\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,dx\,dz & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2}2z{x}^{2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,dx]dz \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{[\frac{2}{3}\,z{x}^{3}+x\operatorname{ln}⁡3]}_{x=0}^{x=2}\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{2}{3}\,z(8-0)+(2-0)\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{16}{3}\,z+2\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{16}{3}z+2\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,dz & ={[\frac{8}{3}{z}^{2}+2z\operatorname{ln}⁡3]}_{z=-1}^{z=1} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}(1-1)+2(1-(-1))\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡3\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By integrating first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,dV
$$

over the rectangular box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \pi ,\,0\le z\le \pi }.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,dy\,dz\,dx
$$

Since we're integrating first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x,$ we write $\text{d}V=\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y+z)]_{0}^{\pi }\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z+\pi )+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z+0)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z)\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z)\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi }2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z)\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2[\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+z)]_{z=0}^{z=\pi }\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+0))\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,dx \\  & =-4{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-4{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx & =4[\operatorname{cos}⁡x]_{x=0}^{x=\pi /2} \\  & =4(0-1) \\  & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}2x+3{y}^{2}+4{z}^{3}\,dV
$$

over the rectangular box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 2,\,0\le z\le 1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}2x+3{y}^{2}+4{z}^{3}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}2x+3{y}^{2}+4{z}^{3}\,dx\,dy\,dz
$$

Since we're integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z,$ we write $\text{d}V=\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}2x+3{y}^{2}+4{z}^{3}\,dx\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{3}2x+3{y}^{2}+4{z}^{3}\,dx]dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{x}^{2}+(3{y}^{2}+4{z}^{3})x]_{x=0}^{x=3}\,dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}(9-0)+(3{y}^{2}+4{z}^{3})(3-0)\,dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}9+9{y}^{2}+12{z}^{3}\,dy\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $z$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}9+9{y}^{2}+12{z}^{3}\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2}9+12{z}^{3}+9{y}^{2}\,dy]dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[(9+12{z}^{3})y+3{y}^{3}]_{y=0}^{y=2}\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(9+12{z}^{3})(2-0)+3(8-0)\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}18+24{z}^{3}+24\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}42+24{z}^{3}\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}42+24{z}^{3}\,dz & =[42z+6{z}^{4}]_{z=0}^{z=1} \\  & =42(1-0)+6(1-0) \\  & =48\end{aligned}
$$
